questiontext.text: What does each node in a singly linked list contain?

answer.text: The data plus a next pointer to the following node

feedback.text: Correct — a payload and one forward link.

answer.text: The data plus a numeric array index

feedback.text: Linked nodes chain by pointer, not by index.

answer.text: The data plus both a prev and a next pointer

feedback.text: That describes a doubly linked list node.

answer.text: Only the data, with no link field

feedback.text: Without a link the nodes could not form a chain.

generalfeedback.text: A singly linked node holds its data and exactly one next pointer.

questiontext.text: Given a pointer to the node just before the target, what is the cost of inserting or deleting a node?

feedback.text: Correct — only a couple of pointers are rewired, with no shifting.
No shifting is needed once you already have the position.
There is no logarithmic work in relinking a node.
That is unrelated to a local pointer update.

generalfeedback.text: At a known position, insertion and deletion just relink pointers in constant time.

questiontext.text: What is the time complexity of searching for a value in a singly linked list?

feedback.text: Correct — you must traverse node by node from the head.
A linked list has no random access, so lookup is not constant time.
Binary search needs random access, which a linked list lacks.
A single linear scan is O(n), not O(n log n).

generalfeedback.text: Because there is no random access, finding a value means a sequential O(n) scan.

questiontext.text: How do you traverse a singly linked list?

answer.text: Start at the head and follow each next pointer in turn

feedback.text: Correct — sequential traversal from the head.

answer.text: Compute each element's address from its index

feedback.text: That works for arrays, not linked lists.

answer.text: Begin at the tail and follow prev pointers backward

feedback.text: A singly linked list has no prev pointers.

answer.text: Use binary search to jump to the middle

feedback.text: Binary search needs random access, which is unavailable here.

generalfeedback.text: You walk the chain from the head, following next until you reach the end.

questiontext.text: Which statements about a singly linked list are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Insertion or deletion at a known node is O(1) with no shifting

feedback.text: Yes — just relink a few pointers.

answer.text: It does not support O(1) random access

feedback.text: Yes — reaching an element requires traversal.

answer.text: You can jump to the k-th element in O(1)

feedback.text: No — reaching the k-th node takes O(k) traversal.

answer.text: Elements are stored contiguously in memory

feedback.text: No — nodes are scattered and linked by pointers.

generalfeedback.text: Linked lists trade O(1) random access for O(1) local insert/delete and no shifting.

questiontext.text: A singly linked list can insert at a known position in O(1) without shifting any elements.

feedback.text: Correct — inserting only relinks pointers, with no shifting.
It really is O(1) at a known position; no elements move.

questiontext.text: A singly linked list supports O(1) random access to any element by its index.

feedback.text: Reaching an arbitrary element requires O(n) traversal from the head.
Correct — a linked list has no O(1) random access.

questiontext.text: Each node in a singly linked list refers to the following node through a ______.

feedback.text: Correct — a pointer (the next field) links the nodes.
Correct — a pointer (the next field) links the nodes.
Correct — the next pointer links to the following node.
Correct — the next pointer links to the following node.
